shloka_text: ततस्ताँल्लक्ष्य वित्रस्तान्यक्षेन्द्रांश्च सहस्रशः । धनाध्यक्षो महायक्षं माणिचारमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.15.1 ।।
transliteration: tatastāँllakṣya vitrastānyakṣendrāṃśca sahasraśaḥ | dhanādhyakṣo mahāyakṣaṃ māṇicāramathābravīt || 7.15.1 ||
translation: ततः then, तान् them, लक्ष्य having seen, वित्रस्तान् terrified, यक्षेन्द्रान् the chief Yakshas, च and, सहस्रशः by thousands, धनाध्यक्षः the lord of wealth, महायक्षम् to the great Yaksha, माणिचारम् Manichara, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then, the lord of wealth, having seen those thousands of terrified chief Yakshas, spoke to the great Yaksha Manichara.
comments: Kubera sends Manibhadra and fresh Yaksha forces, but they are slain in thousands -- Manibhadra duels Ravana and knocks his crown askew -- Kubera himself comes, rebukes Ravana with counsel on righteousness and fights him, but Ravana, resorting to illusion, fells him with a mace -- victorious, Ravana seizes the Pushpaka chariot and, swollen with pride, descends from Kailasa believing he has conquered the three worlds.

shloka_text: रावणं जहि यक्षेन्द्र दुर्वृत्तं पापचेतसम् । शरणं भव वीराणां यक्षाणां युद्धशालिनाम् ।। 7.15.2 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaṃ jahi yakṣendra durvṛttaṃ pāpacetasam | śaraṇaṃ bhava vīrāṇāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ yuddhaśālinām || 7.15.2 ||
translation: रावणम् Ravana, जहि kill, यक्षेन्द्र O chief of Yakshas, दुर्वृत्तम् ill-behaved, पापचेतसम् evil-minded, शरणम् refuge, भव be, वीराणाम् for the brave ones, यक्षाणाम् for the Yakshas, युद्धशालिनाम् who are skilled in battle.
explanation: O chief of Yakshas, kill the ill-behaved and evil-minded Ravana, and be a refuge for these brave Yakshas skilled in battle.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्माणिभद्रः सुदुर्जयः । वृतो यक्षसहस्रैस्तु चतुर्भिः समयोधयत् ।। 7.15.3 ।।
transliteration: evamukto mahābāhurmāṇibhadraḥ sudurjayaḥ | vṛto yakṣasahasraistu caturbhiḥ samayodhayat || 7.15.3 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः addressed, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, माणिभद्रः Manibhadra, सुदुर्जयः very difficult to conquer, वृतः surrounded, यक्षसहस्रैः by thousands of Yakshas, तु indeed, चतुर्भिः by four (thousands), समयोधयत् he fought.
explanation: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed Manibhadra, who was very difficult to conquer, surrounded by four thousand Yakshas, then engaged in battle.

shloka_text: ते गदामुसलप्रासैः शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः । अभिघ्नन्तस्तदा यक्षा राक्षसान्समुपाद्रवन् ।। 7.15.4 ।।
transliteration: te gadāmusalaprāsaiḥ śaktitomaramudgaraiḥ | abhighnantastadā yakṣā rākṣasānsamupādravan || 7.15.4 ||
translation: ते they, गदामुसलप्रासैः with maces, pestles, and spears, शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः with lances, javelins, and hammers, अभिघ्नन्तः striking, तदा then, यक्षाः the Yakshas, राक्षसान् towards the Rakshasas, समुपाद्रवन् rushed
explanation: Then, the Yakshas, striking with maces, pestles, spears, lances, javelins, and hammers, rushed towards the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तस्तुमुलं युद्धं चरन्तः श्येनवल्लघु । बाढं प्रयच्छन्नेच्छामि दीयतामिति भाषिणः ।। 7.15.5 ।।
transliteration: kurvantastumulaṃ yuddhaṃ carantaḥ śyenavallaghu | bāḍhaṃ prayacchannecchāmi dīyatāmiti bhāṣiṇaḥ || 7.15.5 ||
translation: कुर्वन्तः doing, तुमुलम् tumultuous, युद्धम् battle, चरन्तः moving, श्येनवत् like a hawk, लघु swiftly, बाढम् fiercely, प्रयच्छन् giving (blows), न not, इच्छामि I wish (to stop), दीयताम् let it be given (the fight), इति thus, भाषिणः speaking
explanation: They engaged in a tumultuous battle, moving swiftly like hawks, giving fierce blows and speaking as if to say, "I do not wish to stop, let the fight be given!"

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः । दृष्ट्वा तत्तुमुलं युद्धं परं विस्मयमागमन् ।। 7.15.6 ।।
transliteration: tato devāḥ sagandharvā ṛṣayo brahmavādinaḥ | dṛṣṭvā tattumulaṃ yuddhaṃ paraṃ vismayamāgaman || 7.15.6 ||
translation: ततः then, देवाः the gods, सगन्धर्वाः with Gandharvas, ऋषयः the sages, ब्रह्मवादिनः who expound the Vedas, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तत् that, तुमुलम् tumultuous, युद्धम् battle, परम् great, विस्मयम् wonder, आगमन् attained
explanation: Then, the gods along with the Gandharvas, and the sages who expound the Vedas, having witnessed that tumultuous battle, were filled with great wonder.

shloka_text: यक्षाणां तु प्रहस्तेन सहस्रं निहतं रणे । महोदरेण चानिन्द्यं सहस्रमपरं हतम् ।। 7.15.7 ।।
transliteration: yakṣāṇāṃ tu prahastena sahasraṃ nihataṃ raṇe | mahodareṇa cānindyaṃ sahasramaparaṃ hatam || 7.15.7 ||
translation: यक्षाणाम् of the Yakshas, तु indeed, प्रहस्तेन by Prahasta, सहस्रम् a thousand, निहतम् slain, रणे in battle, महोदरेण by Mahodara, च and, अनिन्द्यम् blameless (warriors), सहस्रम् a thousand, अपरम् another, हतम् slain
explanation: Indeed, a thousand Yakshas were slain in battle by Prahasta, and another thousand blameless (excellent) Yaksha warriors were slain by Mahodara.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धेन च तदा राजन्मारीचेन युयुत्सुना । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्रे निपातिते ।। 7.15.8 ।।
transliteration: kruddhena ca tadā rājanmārīcena yuyutsunā | nimeṣāntaramātreṇa dve sahasre nipātite || 7.15.8 ||
translation: क्रुद्धेन by the enraged, च and, तदा then, राजन् O King, मारीचेन by Maricha, युयुत्सुना who desired to fight, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in merely the twinkling of an eye, द्वे सहस्रे two thousand, निपातिते struck down
explanation: And then, O King, by the enraged Maricha, who desired to fight, two thousand (Yakshas) were struck down in merely the twinkling of an eye.

shloka_text: क्व च यक्षार्जवं युद्धं क्व च मायाबलाश्रयम् । रक्षसां पुरुषव्याघ्र तेन ते ऽभ्यधिका युधि ।। 7.15.9 ।।
transliteration: kva ca yakṣārjavaṃ yuddhaṃ kva ca māyābalāśrayam | rakṣasāṃ puruṣavyāghra tena te 'bhyadhikā yudhi || 7.15.9 ||
translation: क्व च where also, यक्षार्जवं the straightforwardness of the Yakshas, युद्धं battle, क्व च where also, मायाबलाश्रयम् reliance on illusory power, रक्षसां of the Rakshasas, पुरुषव्याघ्र O tiger among men, तेन by that, ते they, अभ्यधिका superior, युधि in battle.
explanation: O tiger among men, how can the straightforward battle of the Yakshas compare with the Rakshasas' reliance on magical power, which is why the Rakshasas are superior in war.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे । मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात्तडितो न च कम्पितः ।। 7.15.10 ।।
transliteration: dhūmrākṣeṇa samāgamya māṇibhadro mahāraṇe | musalenorasi krodhāttaḍito na ca kampitaḥ || 7.15.10 ||
translation: धूम्राक्षेण by Dhūmrākṣa, समागम्य having met, माणिभद्रो Maṇibhadra, महारणे in the great battle, मुसलेन with a mace, उरसि on the chest, क्रोधात् with anger, ताडितो struck, न च and not, कम्पितः trembled.
explanation: In the great battle, Maṇibhadra, having encountered Dhūmrākṣa, was struck on the chest with a mace by him in anger, yet he did not even tremble.

shloka_text: ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः । धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलः स पपात ह ।। 7.15.11 ।।
transliteration: tato gadāṃ samāvidhya māṇibhadreṇa rākṣasaḥ | dhūmrākṣastāḍito mūrdhni vihvalaḥ sa papāta ha || 7.15.11 ||
translation: ततो then, गदां a mace, समाविध्य having brandished, माणिभद्रेण by Maṇibhadra, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, धूम्राक्षः Dhūmrākṣa, ताडितो struck, मूर्ध्नि on the head, विह्वलः bewildered, स he, पपात ह indeed fell.
explanation: Then, Maṇibhadra, having brandished his mace, struck the Rakshasa Dhūmrākṣa on the head, and he, bewildered, indeed fell.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम् । अभ्यधावत सङ्ग्रामे माणिभद्रं दशाननः ।। 7.15.12 ।।
transliteration: dhūmrākṣaṃ tāḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ śoṇitokṣitam | abhyadhāvata saṅgrāme māṇibhadraṃ daśānanaḥ || 7.15.12 ||
translation: धूम्राक्षं Dhūmrākṣa, ताडितं struck, दृष्ट्वा having seen, पतितं fallen, शोणितोक्षितम् drenched in blood, अभ्यधावत rushed towards, सङ्ग्रामे in battle, माणिभद्रं Maṇibhadra, दशाननः Daśānana.
explanation: Having seen Dhūmrākṣa struck, fallen, and drenched in blood, Daśānana rushed towards Maṇibhadra in battle.

shloka_text: तं क्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं माणिभद्रो दशाननम् । शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुङ्गवः ।। 7.15.13 ।।
transliteration: taṃ kruddhamabhidhāvantaṃ māṇibhadro daśānanam | śaktibhistāḍayāmāsa tisṛbhiryakṣapuṅgavaḥ || 7.15.13 ||
translation: तं him, क्रुद्धम् angry, अभिधावन्तं rushing towards, माणिभद्रो Maṇibhadra, दशाननम् Daśānana, शक्तिभिः with spears, ताडयामास struck, तिसृभिः with three, यक्षपुङ्गवः the foremost among Yakshas.
explanation: The foremost among Yakshas, Maṇibhadra, struck that angry Daśānana, who was rushing towards him, with three spears.

shloka_text: ताडितो माणिभद्रस्य मुकुटे प्राहरद्रणे । तस्य तेन प्रहारेम मुकुटं पार्श्वमागतम् ।। 7.15.14 ।।
transliteration: tāḍito māṇibhadrasya mukuṭe prāharadraṇe | tasya tena prahārema mukuṭaṃ pārśvamāgatam || 7.15.14 ||
translation: ताडितो being struck, माणिभद्रस्य of Manibhadra, मुकुटे on the crown, प्राहरत् he struck, रणे in battle, तस्य his, तेन by that, प्रहारेण by the blow, मुकुटं the crown, पार्श्वम् to the side, आगतम् came.
explanation: Being struck, he then struck Manibhadra's crown in battle, and by that blow, his crown was knocked to the side.

shloka_text: ततः संयुध्यमानेन विष्टब्धो न व्यकम्पत । तदाप्रभृति यक्षो ऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरिति स्मृतः । सन्नादः सुमहान्राजंस्तस्मिन्शैले ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.15.15 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ saṃyudhyamānena viṣṭabdho na vyakampata | tadāprabhṛti yakṣo 'sau pārśvamauliriti smṛtaḥ | sannādaḥ sumahānrājaṃstasminśaile 'bhyavartata || 7.15.15 ||
translation: ततः then, संयुध्यमानेन by one who was fighting, विष्टब्धो firm, न not, व्यकम्पत he trembled, तदाप्रभृति from that time onwards, यक्षो the Yaksha, असौ that, पार्श्वमौलिः one with a side-tilted crown, इति thus, स्मृतः is known, सन्नादः a great roar, सुमहान् very great, राजन् O King, तस्मिन् on that, शैले mountain, अभ्यवर्तत resounded.
explanation: Then, though fighting, he remained firm and did not tremble, and from that time onwards, that Yaksha became known as Pārśvamauli (one with a side-tilted crown); O King, a very great roar resounded on that mountain.

shloka_text: ततो दूरात्प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः । शुक्रप्रौष्ठपदाभ्यां च पद्मशङ्खसमावृतः ।। 7.15.16 ।।
transliteration: tato dūrātpradadṛśe dhanādhyakṣo gadādharaḥ | śukraprauṣṭhapadābhyāṃ ca padmaśaṅkhasamāvṛtaḥ || 7.15.16 ||
translation: ततः then, दूरात् from afar, प्रददृशे was seen, धनाध्यक्षो the lord of wealth, गदाधरः the mace-wielder, शुक्रप्रौष्ठपदाभ्यां by Shukra and Praushthapada, च and, पद्मशङ्खसमावृतः surrounded by Padma and Shankha.
explanation: Then, from afar, the mace-wielding lord of wealth (Kubera) was seen, accompanied by Shukra and Praushthapada, and surrounded by Padma and Shankha.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं सङ्ख्ये शापाद्विभ्रष्टगौरवम् । उवाच वचनं धीमान्युक्तं पैतामहे कुले ।। 7.15.17 ।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ saṅkhye śāpādvibhraṣṭagauravam | uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmānyuktaṃ paitāmahe kule || 7.15.17 ||
translation: सः he, दृष्ट्वा having seen, भ्रातरं his brother, सङ्ख्ये in battle, शापात् due to a curse, विभ्रष्टगौरवम् whose glory was lost, उवाच spoke, वचनं words, धीमान् the wise one, युक्तं appropriate, पैतामहे in the paternal, कुले family.
explanation: Having seen his brother in battle, whose glory was lost due to a curse, the wise Kubera spoke words appropriate for their paternal lineage.

shloka_text: यन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं नावगच्छसि दुर्मते । पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः ।। 7.15.18 ।।
transliteration: yanmayā vāryamāṇastvaṃ nāvagacchasi durmate | paścādasya phalaṃ prāpya jñāsyase nirayaṃ gataḥ || 7.15.18 ||
translation: यत् because, मया by me, वार्यमाणः being restrained, त्वं you, न not, अवगच्छसि understand, दुर्मते O evil-minded one, पश्चात् afterwards, अस्य of this, फलं the fruit, प्राप्य having obtained, ज्ञास्यसे you will know, निरयं to hell, गतः having gone.
explanation: O evil-minded one, because you do not understand even when restrained by me, you will realize the consequence of this after having gone to hell.

shloka_text: यो हि मोहाद्विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति दुर्मतिः । स तस्य परिणामान्ते जानीते कर्मणः फलम् ।। 7.15.19 ।।
transliteration: yo hi mohādviṣaṃ pītvā nāvagacchati durmatiḥ | sa tasya pariṇāmānte jānīte karmaṇaḥ phalam || 7.15.19 ||
translation: यः who, हि indeed, मोहात् from delusion, विषम् poison, पीत्वा having drunk, न not, अवगच्छति understands, दुर्मतिः the evil-minded one, सः he, तस्य its, परिणामान्ते at the end of the consequence, जानीते knows, कर्मणः of the action, फलम् the fruit.
explanation: An evil-minded person who, out of delusion, drinks poison and does not understand its nature, will only realize the consequence of that action at its ultimate fruition.

shloka_text: देवता नाभिनन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तेन केनचित् । येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्सन्नावबुद्ध्यसे ।। 7.15.20 ।।
transliteration: devatā nābhinandanti dharmayuktena kenacit | yena tvamīdṛśaṃ bhāvaṃ nītassannāvabuddhyase || 7.15.20 ||
translation: देवताः gods, न not, अभिनन्दन्ति approve, धर्मयुक्तेन by one endowed with righteousness, केनचित् by anyone, येन by which, त्वम् you, ईदृशम् such, भावम् state, नीतः सन् having been brought, न not, अवबुद्ध्यसे understand.
explanation: The gods do not approve of such a state, nor does any righteous person, by which you have been brought to this condition and yet do not understand it.

shloka_text: मातरं पितरं यो हि आचार्यं चावमन्यते । स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः ।। 7.15.21 ।।
transliteration: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ yo hi ācāryaṃ cāvamanyate | sa paśyati phalaṃ tasya pretarājavaśaṃ gataḥ || 7.15.21 ||
translation: मातरम् mother, पितरम् father, यः who, हि indeed, आचार्यम् teacher, च and, अवमन्यते disrespects, सः he, पश्यति sees, फलम् the fruit, तस्य of that, प्रेतराजवशम् under the sway of the king of the dead, गतः having gone.
explanation: Indeed, whoever disrespects their mother, father, and teacher will see the consequences of such actions after falling under the dominion of Yama, the king of the dead.

shloka_text: अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोर्जनम् । स पश्चात्तप्यते मूढो मृतो दृष्ट्वा ऽ ऽत्मनो गतिम् ।। 7.15.22 ।।
transliteration: adhruve hi śarīre yo na karoti taporjanam | sa paścāttapyate mūḍho mṛto dṛṣṭvā ' 'tmano gatim || 7.15.22 ||
translation: अध्रुवे in the impermanent, हि indeed, शरीरे body, यः who, न not, करोति does, तपः अर्जनम् acquisition of penance, सः he, पश्चात् afterwards, तप्यते repents, मूढः the foolish one, मृतः having died, दृष्ट्वा having seen, आत्मनः of oneself, गतिम् the destination.
explanation: Indeed, the foolish person who does not accumulate merit through penance in this impermanent body will repent later, after death, upon seeing their own ultimate destination.

shloka_text: धर्माद्राज्यं धनं सौख्यमधर्माद्दुःखमेव च । तस्माद्धर्मं सुखार्थाय कुर्यात्पापं विसर्जयेत् ।। 7.15.23 ।।
transliteration: dharmādrājyaṃ dhanaṃ saukhyamadharmādduḥkhameva ca | tasmāddharmaṃ sukhārthāya kuryātpāpaṃ visarjayet || 7.15.23 ||
translation: धर्मात् from righteousness, राज्यम् kingdom, धनम् wealth, सौख्यम् happiness, अधर्मात् from unrighteousness, दुःखम् sorrow, एव only, च and, तस्मात् therefore, धर्मम् righteousness, सुखार्थाय for the sake of happiness, कुर्यात् one should do, पापम् sin, विसर्जयेत् one should abandon.
explanation: From righteousness come kingdom, wealth, and happiness, while from unrighteousness comes only sorrow; therefore, one should practice righteousness for the sake of happiness and abandon sin.

shloka_text: पापस्य हि फलं दुःखं तद्भोक्तव्यमिहात्मना । तस्मादात्मापघातार्थं मूढः पापं करिष्यति ।। 7.15.24 ।।
transliteration: pāpasya hi phalaṃ duḥkhaṃ tadbhoktavyamihātmanā | tasmādātmāpaghātārthaṃ mūḍhaḥ pāpaṃ kariṣyati || 7.15.24 ||
translation: पापस्य of sin, हि indeed, फलम् the fruit, दुःखम् is sorrow, तत् that, भोक्तव्यम् must be experienced, इह here, आत्मना by oneself; तस्मात् therefore, आत्म self, अपघातार्थम् for the destruction, मूढः a fool, पापम् sin, करिष्यति will commit.
explanation: Indeed, the fruit of sin is sorrow, which one must experience oneself in this world; therefore, only a fool would commit sin for the purpose of self-destruction.

shloka_text: कस्य चिन्न हि दुर्बुद्धेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः । देवं चेष्टयते सर्वं हतो दैवेन हन्यते । यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते ।। 7.15.25 ।।
transliteration: kasya cinna hi durbuddheśchandato jāyate matiḥ | devaṃ ceṣṭayate sarvaṃ hato daivena hanyate | yādṛśaṃ kurute karma tādṛśaṃ phalamaśnute || 7.15.25 ||
translation: कस्यचित् of anyone, न not, हि indeed, दुर्बुद्धेः of an evil-minded person, छन्दतः by one's own will, जायते arises, मतिः the intellect; दैवम् destiny, चेष्टयते directs, सर्वम् everything; हतः one who is struck, दैवेन by fate, हन्यते is destroyed; यादृशम् whatever kind of, कुरुते one performs, कर्म action, तादृशम् that kind of, फलम् fruit, अश्नुते one obtains.
explanation: Indeed, the intellect of an evil-minded person does not arise by their own will, for destiny directs everything, and one struck by fate is destroyed, ultimately receiving the fruit corresponding to the actions one performs.

shloka_text: बुद्धिरूपं फलं पुत्राञ्छौर्यं धीरत्वमेव च । प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा लोके निर्जितं पुण्यकर्मभिः ।। 7.15.26 ।।
transliteration: buddhirūpaṃ phalaṃ putrāñchauryaṃ dhīratvameva ca | prāpnuvanti narā loke nirjitaṃ puṇyakarmabhiḥ || 7.15.26 ||
translation: बुद्धि intellect, रूपम् beauty, फलम् prosperity, पुत्रान् sons, शौर्यम् valor, धीरत्वम् steadfastness, एव indeed, च and, प्राप्नुवन्ति obtain, नराः men, लोके in the world, निर्जितम् acquired, पुण्यकर्मभिः by meritorious deeds.
explanation: Men in this world obtain intellect, beauty, prosperity, sons, valor, and steadfastness, all of which are acquired through meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी । न त्वां समभिभाषिष्ये ऽसद्वृत्तेष्वेव निर्णयः ।। 7.15.27 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ nirayagāmī tvaṃ yasya te matirīdṛśī | na tvāṃ samabhibhāṣiṣye 'sadvṛtteṣveva nirṇayaḥ || 7.15.27 ||
translation: एवम् thus, निरयगामी one who goes to hell, त्वम् you, यस्य whose, ते your, मतिः intellect, ईदृशी is such; न not, त्वाम् to you, समभिभाषिष्ये I will speak; असद्वृत्तेषु among those of bad conduct, एव indeed, निर्णयः is the judgment.
explanation: You are destined for hell, as your intellect is of such a nature; I will not speak to you, for such is the judgment for those of bad conduct.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः । मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः ।। 7.15.28 ।।
transliteration: evamuktāstatastena tasyāmātyāḥ samāhatāḥ | mārīcapramukhāḥ sarve vimukhā vipradudruvuḥ || 7.15.28 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ताः spoken to, ततः then, तेन by him, तस्य his, अमात्याः ministers, समाहताः rebuked, मारीचप्रमुखाः Maricha and others, सर्वे all, विमुखाः with averted faces, विप्रदुद्रुवुः fled in all directions.
explanation: Thus rebuked by him, all his ministers, led by Maricha, turned their faces away and fled in all directions.

shloka_text: ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना । गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानात्प्रकम्पितः ।। 7.15.29 ।।
transliteration: tatastena daśagrīvo yakṣendreṇa mahātmanā | gadayābhihato mūrdhni na ca sthānātprakampitaḥ || 7.15.29 ||
translation: ततः then, तेन by him, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, यक्षेन्द्रेण by the lord of Yakshas, महात्मना by the great-souled one, गदया with a mace, अभिहतः struck, मूर्ध्नि on the head, न not, च and, स्थानात् from his place, प्रकम्पितः shaken
explanation: Then, the great-souled lord of Yakshas struck Dashagriva on the head with a mace, but Ravana was not shaken from his position.

shloka_text: ततस्तौ राम निघ्नन्तौ तदान्योन्यं महामृधे । न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ बभूवतुरमर्षणौ ।। 7.15.30 ।।
transliteration: tatastau rāma nighnantau tadānyonyaṃ mahāmṛdhe | na vihvalau na ca śrāntau babhūvaturamarṣaṇau || 7.15.30 ||
translation: ततः then, तौ those two, राम O Rama, निघ्नन्तौ striking, तदा then, अन्योन्यम् each other, महामृधे in the great battle, न not, विह्वलौ distressed, न not, च and, श्रान्तौ weary, बभूवतुः became, अमर्षणौ furious
explanation: O Rama, then those two, striking each other in that great battle, became neither distressed nor weary, but remained furious.

shloka_text: आग्नेयमस्त्रं तस्मै स मुमोच धनदस्तदा । राक्षसेन्द्रो वारुणेन तदस्त्रं प्रत्यवारयत् ।। 7.15.31 ।।
transliteration: āgneyamastraṃ tasmai sa mumoca dhanadastadā | rākṣasendro vāruṇena tadastraṃ pratyavārayat || 7.15.31 ||
translation: आग्नेयम् fiery, अस्त्रम् weapon, तस्मै at him, सः he, मुमोच released, धनदः Dhanada, तदा then, राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of Rakshasas, वारुणेन with the Varuna weapon, तत् that, अस्त्रम् weapon, प्रत्यवारयत् countered
explanation: Then Dhanada released the fiery weapon at him, but the lord of Rakshasas countered that weapon with the Varuna weapon.

shloka_text: ततो मायां प्रविष्टो ऽसौ राक्षसीं राक्षसेश्वरः । रूपाणां शतसाहस्रं विनाशाय चकार च ।। 7.15.32 ।।
transliteration: tato māyāṃ praviṣṭo 'sau rākṣasīṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ | rūpāṇāṃ śatasāhasraṃ vināśāya cakāra ca || 7.15.32 ||
translation: ततः then, मायाम् illusion, प्रविष्टः entered, असौ that, राक्षसीम् demonic, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas, रूपाणाम् of forms, शतसाहस्रम् a hundred thousand, विनाशाय for destruction, चकार made, च and
explanation: Then, that lord of Rakshasas entered into a demonic illusion and created a hundred thousand forms for destruction.

shloka_text: व्याघ्रो वराहो जीमूतः पर्वतः सागरो द्रुमः । यक्षो दैत्यस्वरूपी च सो ऽदृश्यत दशाननः ।। 7.15.33 ।।
transliteration: vyāghro varāho jīmūtaḥ parvataḥ sāgaro drumaḥ | yakṣo daityasvarūpī ca so 'dṛśyata daśānanaḥ || 7.15.33 ||
translation: व्याघ्रः a tiger, वराहः a boar, जीमूतः a cloud, पर्वतः a mountain, सागरः an ocean, द्रुमः a tree, यक्षः a Yaksha, दैत्यस्वरूपी having the form of a Daitya, च and, सः he, अदृश्यत was seen, दशाननः Dashanana
explanation: Dashanana was then seen in the forms of a tiger, a boar, a cloud, a mountain, an ocean, a tree, a Yaksha, and a Daitya.

shloka_text: बहूनि च करोति स्म दृश्यन्ते न त्वसौ ततः । प्रतिगृह्य ततो राम महदस्त्रं दशाननः ।। 7.15.34 ।।
transliteration: bahūni ca karoti sma dṛśyante na tvasau tataḥ | pratigṛhya tato rāma mahadastraṃ daśānanaḥ || 7.15.34 ||
translation: बहूनि many, च and, करोति स्म was doing, दृश्यन्ते are seen, न not, तु indeed, असौ he (Ravana), ततः from that, प्रतिगृह्य having received, ततो then, राम O Rama, महत् great, अस्त्रम् weapon, दशाननः Ravana.
explanation: Ravana, having received a great weapon, was performing many actions, but he himself was not visible.

shloka_text: जघान मूर्ध्नि धनदं व्याविद्ध्य महतीं गदाम् । एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः ।। 7.15.35 ।।
transliteration: jaghāna mūrdhni dhanadaṃ vyāviddhya mahatīṃ gadām | evaṃ sa tenābhihato vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ || 7.15.35 ||
translation: जघान struck, मूर्ध्नि on the head, धनदम् Kubera, व्याविद्ध्य having whirled, महतीम् great, गदाम् mace, एवम् thus, सः he (Kubera), तेन by him (Ravana), अभिहतः struck, विह्वलः bewildered, शोणितोक्षितः drenched in blood.
explanation: Having whirled a great mace, Ravana struck Kubera on the head, and thus Kubera, bewildered and drenched in blood, was struck by him.

shloka_text: कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः ।। 7.15.36 ।।
transliteration: kṛttamūla ivāśoko nipapāta dhanādhipaḥ || 7.15.36 ||
translation: कृत्तमूलः with roots cut, इव like, अशोकः an Ashoka tree, निपपात fell down, धनाधिपः the lord of wealth (Kubera).
explanation: The lord of wealth, Kubera, fell down like an Ashoka tree whose roots had been cut.

shloka_text: ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स तदा वृतः । धनदोच्छ्वासितस्तैस्तु वनमानीय नन्दनम् ।। 7.15.37 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ padmādibhistatra nidhibhiḥ sa tadā vṛtaḥ | dhanadocchvāsitastaistu vanamānīya nandanam || 7.15.37 ||
translation: ततः then, पद्मादिभिः by Padma and others, तत्र there, निधिभिः by the treasures, सः he (Kubera), तदा then, वृतः surrounded, धनदः Kubera, उच्छ्वासितः revived, तैस्तु by them, वनम् to the forest, आनीय having brought, नन्दनम् Nandana.
explanation: Then, surrounded by the treasures like Padma and others, Kubera was revived by them and brought to the Nandana forest.

shloka_text: निर्जित्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्तं धनदं हृष्टमानसः । पुष्पकं तस्य जग्राह विमानं जयलक्षणम् ।। 7.15.38 ।।
transliteration: nirjitya rākṣasendrastaṃ dhanadaṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ | puṣpakaṃ tasya jagrāha vimānaṃ jayalakṣaṇam || 7.15.38 ||
translation: निर्जित्य having conquered, राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of Rakshasas (Ravana), तम् him, धनदम् Kubera, हृष्टमानसः with a joyful mind, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, तस्य his, जग्राह took, विमानम् aerial chariot, जयलक्षणम् marked by victory.
explanation: Having conquered Kubera, the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, with a joyful mind, took his Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was a symbol of victory.

shloka_text: काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं वैडूर्यमणितोरणम् । मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं सर्वकामफलद्रुमम् ।। 7.15.39 ।।
transliteration: kāñcanastambhasaṃvītaṃ vaiḍūryamaṇitoraṇam | muktājālapraticchannaṃ sarvakāmaphaladrumam || 7.15.39 ||
translation: काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं surrounded by golden pillars, वैडूर्यमणितोरणम् with archways of cat's eye gems, मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं covered with nets of pearls, सर्वकामफलद्रुमम् a wish-fulfilling tree.
explanation: The Pushpaka Vimana was adorned with golden pillars, archways made of cat's eye gems, and covered with nets of pearls, resembling a wish-fulfilling tree that grants all desires.

shloka_text: मनोजवं कामगमं कामरूपं विहङ्गमम् । मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् ।। 7.15.40 ।।
transliteration: manojavaṃ kāmagamaṃ kāmarūpaṃ vihaṅgamam | maṇikāñcanasopānaṃ taptakāñcanavedikam || 7.15.40 ||
translation: मनोजवं swift as thought, कामगमं moving at will, कामरूपं changing form at will, विहङ्गमम् a flying vehicle, मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं with stairs of gems and gold, तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् with platforms of refined gold.
explanation: This flying vehicle was swift as thought, could move and change its form at will, and featured stairs made of gems and gold, along with platforms of refined gold.

shloka_text: देवोपवाह्यमक्षय्यं सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम् । बह्वाश्चर्यं भक्तिचित्रं ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितम् ।। 7.15.41 ।।
transliteration: devopavāhyamakṣayyaṃ sadādṛṣṭimanaḥsukham | bahvāścaryaṃ bhakticitraṃ brahmaṇā parinirmitam || 7.15.41 ||
translation: देवोपवाह्यम a vehicle for gods, अक्षय्यं imperishable, सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम् always pleasing to sight and mind, बह्वाश्चर्यं full of many wonders, भक्तिचित्रं wonderfully adorned, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, परिनिर्मितम् perfectly created.
explanation: This imperishable vehicle, created perfectly by Brahma, was fit for gods, always pleasing to the eyes and mind, and wonderfully adorned with many marvels.

shloka_text: निर्मितं सर्वकामैस्तु मनोहरमनुत्तमम् । न तु शीतं न चोष्णं च सर्वर्तुसुखदं शुभम् ।। 7.15.42 ।।
transliteration: nirmitaṃ sarvakāmaistu manoharamanuttamam | na tu śītaṃ na coṣṇaṃ ca sarvartusukhadaṃ śubham || 7.15.42 ||
translation: निर्मितं created, सर्वकामैस्तु indeed with all desired comforts, मनोहरम captivating the mind, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed, न तु शीतं neither cold, न चोष्णं nor hot, च and, सर्वर्तुसुखदं giving comfort in all seasons, शुभम् auspicious.
explanation: It was an unsurpassed, mind-captivating creation, endowed with all desired comforts, neither cold nor hot, providing pleasantness in all seasons, and truly auspicious.

shloka_text: स तं राजा समारुह्य कामगं वीर्यनिर्जितम् । जितं त्रिभुवनं मेने दर्पोत्सेकात्सुदुर्मतिः ।। 7.15.43 ।।
transliteration: sa taṃ rājā samāruhya kāmagaṃ vīryanirjitam | jitaṃ tribhuvanaṃ mene darpotsekātsudurmatiḥ || 7.15.43 ||
translation: स He, तं that, राजा king (Ravana), समारुह्य having ascended, कामगं moving at will, वीर्यनिर्जितम् conquered by his prowess, जितं conquered, त्रिभुवनं the three worlds, मेने he thought, दर्पोत्सेकात् due to excessive pride, सुदुर्मतिः the very foolish one.
explanation: Having ascended that wish-fulfilling vehicle, which he had conquered by his prowess, the very foolish King Ravana, swollen with excessive pride, believed he had conquered the three worlds.

shloka_text: जित्वा वैश्रवणं देवं कैलासात्समवातरत् ।। 7.15.44 ।।
transliteration: jitvā vaiśravaṇaṃ devaṃ kailāsātsamavātarat || 7.15.44 ||
translation: जित्वा having conquered, वैश्रवणं Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), देवं the god, कैलासात् from Kailasa, समवातरत् descended.
explanation: Having conquered the god Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), he descended from Mount Kailasa.

shloka_text: स्वतेजसा विपुलमवाप्य तं जयं प्रतापवान्विमलकिरीटहारवान् । रराज वै परमविमानमास्थितो निशाचरः सदसि गतो यथानलः ।। 7.15.45 ।।
transliteration: svatejasā vipulamavāpya taṃ jayaṃ pratāpavānvimalakirīṭahāravān | rarāja vai paramavimānamāsthito niśācaraḥ sadasi gato yathānalaḥ || 7.15.45 ||
translation: स्वतेजसा by his own prowess, विपुलम् great, अवाप्य having obtained, तं that, जयं victory, प्रतापवान् the mighty one, विमलकिरीटहारवान् adorned with a spotless crown and necklace, रराज shone, वै indeed, परमविमानम् the excellent aerial chariot, आस्थितः having mounted, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (Rakshasa), सदसि in an assembly, गतः present, यथा like, अनलः fire.
explanation: Having achieved that great victory by his own prowess, the mighty Rakshasa, adorned with a spotless crown and necklace, shone brightly while seated in the excellent aerial chariot, like fire present in an assembly. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः ।। 15 ।। Thus ends the fifteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
